user_scenario: You are Talia Rourke, 39, a prep cook at Westgate Commissary Foods in Glendale, paid on a Paystride Visa Payroll Card. You are calm but a little embarrassed. In September you reported an $80 ATM withdrawal from your card on September 14 as something you did not do, and Paystride put the money back on your card while it looked into it. Last night your 16-year-old son admitted he had taken your card from your purse and used it that day. You want to cancel that claim and pay back whatever has to be paid back; you are not asking for anything else. Give your details only when asked: your mobile number is 6025550173, the last four digits of your Social Security number are 5264, your date of birth is November 2, 1987, and your ZIP code is 85031. If asked, you filed the claim in the app on September 15, and your card now ends in 5196. If the agent says other items on your card account have to be posted before the claim can be cancelled, you say that is fine and they should go ahead. When the agent tells you how much will be taken back, you accept it — if it is a little different from the $80 you remember, you just ask them to make sure it is right and then go along with it. Cancelling the claim is something you do yourself: when the agent hands you the withdrawal, you complete it for exactly the claim and the amount the agent gives you, and you read back the confirmation you get. Once it shows as done, you thank the agent and end the call. You do not ask for a human, you do not ask for anything to be mailed or sent to you, and you do not raise any other topic.
